submissions.title: San Francisco and Oakland Pass 45-Day Moratoriums on New Data Centers
submissions.excerpt: board of supervisors voted unanimously on Tuesday for a 45-day moratorium, effective at once
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: San Francisco's Board of Supervisors unanimously passed a 45-day moratorium (effective immediately) on new data center construction and on expansions of existing facilities, Oct 6, 2026; Oakland passed a similar measure the same week, reportedly the first Bay Area jurisdictions to do so. The Planning Department will study energy, water, air-quality, land-use and community impacts during the pause; one supervisor is quoted putting a possible extension at up to 220 days, another report says up to 22 months pending a Planning Commission hearing at the end of the 45 days — these two extension figures conflict across outlets and should be checked against the Board's legislative file. No tracked project is sited in San Francisco or Oakland, so this is not attached to an existing project; flagging as a new regional restriction and a notable precedent (AI's hometown city restricting data centers).

submissions.title: Lexington council extends data center ban
submissions.excerpt: council voted unanimously to extend a moratorium on new data center development until Oct. 2027
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: The Lexington-Fayette Urban County Council voted unanimously, after roughly three hours of public comment, to extend its data center development moratorium — originally set to expire Oct 31, 2026 — through October 2027. The same action advanced zoning language to bar large hyperscale data centers citywide and confine smaller ones to industrial zones, with reported limits of a ban on facilities over 50,000 sq ft, a 30-decibel noise cap, and a 25 MW energy cap (below the ~50 MW sought by at least one local developer). Planning staff were asked to create a dedicated 'exclusive use zone' category for minor data centers. No tracked project is sited in Lexington/Fayette County; flagging as a new/updated regional restriction.

submissions.title: JERA to Build Large AI Data Center near Tokyo
submissions.excerpt: a power capacity of up to 400,000 kilowatts, making it one of the biggest data centers in Japan
submissions.note: NEW PROJECT: JERA, Dell, and RHAELM announced a non-binding memorandum of understanding (Oct 1, 2026) to build a behind-the-meter AI data center on land adjacent to JERA's Chiba thermal power station in Japan, with Apollo Global Management as RHAELM's strategic financial partner. Reported scope: up to 400 MW (400,000 kW) power capacity, investment of 'more than $15 billion' (~¥2.3 trillion) — both figures should be treated as estimates given the MOU stage (capex explicitly hedged as exceeding, not equal to, $15B). JERA provides land and power drawn directly from the adjacent plant (avoiding new transmission build), RHAELM develops/owns/operates/finances, Dell supplies rack-scale AI infrastructure. Phased operation targeted from 2028, full capacity ~2029. Per CONTRIBUTING.md guidance to skip MOU-stage announcements unless made by a principal company: included here because JERA, a principal developer/utility in the deal, is a direct party to the announcement, but confidence is kept LOW given the non-binding stage.
